assessment.nobel_worthiness: A decisive materials discovery with exceptional and enduring scientific and technological consequences for modern permanent-magnet applications.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa and Croat are the two credited experimental innovators; the compact attribution is a major strength.
assessment.maturity: The materials class has been extensively reproduced, understood, optimized and deployed over decades.
uncertainties: The boundary between a fundamental physics discovery and a materials-engineering innovation needs careful committee consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance exposed controllable spin-dependent quantum transport and enabled a far-reaching information technology.
assessment.attribution: The three nominees represent foundational observation and the development of practically decisive magnetic tunnel junctions.
assessment.maturity: The effect is quantitatively established, technologically ubiquitous and supported by a mature physical account.
uncertainties: Priority and the appropriate division of credit among parallel experimental and device-development contributions require close historical review.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory made strongly correlated electronic materials quantitatively tractable and transformed the interpretation of their electronic spectra and phases.
assessment.attribution: Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt provide a plausible compact attribution for the central conceptual and methodological advances.
assessment.maturity: The theory is long established, broadly benchmarked and continuously connected to experiment and materials calculations.
uncertainties: The contribution is a powerful theoretical framework rather than one discrete discovery, and its credit history is broad.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defect-mediated melting and the hexatic phase supplied a profound account of phase transitions in two dimensions.
assessment.attribution: The nominees cover central theoretical development and testing, though the wider historical framework must be distinguished carefully.
assessment.maturity: Its predictions have motivated extensive experimental, numerical and theoretical scrutiny over many years.
uncertainties: The exact relation to earlier Kosterlitz-Thouless work and the most appropriate allocation of credit needs careful assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological-insulator framework revealed a robust new class of quantum matter with quantized boundary transport.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the seminal theoretical proposal, while Molenkamp represents decisive experimental establishment.
assessment.maturity: The phenomena are independently reproduced, theoretically coherent and central to contemporary quantum-materials research.
uncertainties: The candidate overlaps conceptually and personally with related topological-insulator and quantum-anomalous-Hall nominations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Photonic band gaps established a compelling analogue of electronic band structure for light and created a durable field of nanophotonics.
assessment.attribution: The credited theorists and experimental pioneer form a coherent representation of the foundational work.
assessment.maturity: The underlying physics is firmly verified and has generated broad experimental and technological consequences.
uncertainties: Practical impact is distributed across many later photonic-crystal developments, complicating a sharply bounded prize citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phase and the Aharonov-Bohm effect changed the physical understanding of phase, gauge potentials and quantum interference.
assessment.attribution: Berry and Aharonov are clear representatives of the two named foundational effects.
assessment.maturity: Both effects have been repeatedly observed and their concepts now permeate quantum materials, optics and precision quantum physics.
uncertainties: The two effects have distinct historical origins, so whether they form one sufficiently unified prize requires judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks achieved an extraordinary advance in frequency metrology and enable stringent tests of fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori and Ye are credible central figures in the proposal, realization and development of the clock architecture.
assessment.maturity: Independent laboratories have reached exceptional performance and the approach is mature enough for precision applications.
uncertainties: The eventual impact on time standards and on uniquely enabled fundamental discoveries is still developing.
